pull.title: feat(analytics): name the coding agent behind every request
pull.body:
## What was reported

> "Analytics don't register requests from OpenCode and other agents? I tried ling-flash-free and
> longcat-2.0-free, they worked but I saw nothing in Analytics. Mention in Analytics what harness
> was used when serving a request — which harnesses requested and we responded to."

## What the log actually said

Checked read-only against `~/.fcc/logs/requests.db` (`mode=ro`, 2.99 GB, 272,293 rows) before a line
was written.

**The OpenCode requests were never missing.** Four rows carry user-agent
`opencode/1.18.26 ai-sdk/provider-utils/4.0.46 runtime/bun/1.3.14`, `POST /v1/messages`,
`provider=nous_portal`, `meituan/longcat-2.0:free`, **all four `success`**, 2026-09-02T14:17:56 ..
22:17:13. They were indistinguishable from the 128,000+ Claude Code rows on the same models, because
nothing in the table, the cards or the detail dialog named the client.

**No `ling` request ever reached MCC.** `resolved_model LIKE '%ling%'` returns zero rows across the
whole log — not a failure, not an error, nothing. A model that appears nowhere in Analytics never
reached the proxy, which is a launcher/base-URL question and not an Analytics one. USAGE now says so
in as many words, because "I saw nothing" has two very different causes and only one of them is a bug
here.

## What this adds

`requests.harness`, filled at capture time from two signals, explicit first.

**1. `x-mcc-harness`**, written by MCC's own launchers into the configuration they generate. Eleven
of the sixteen agents can carry it; each was verified against that CLI's own bundle, vendored schema,
or the wire:

| how | agents |
| --- | --- |
| environment variable | Claude Code (`ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`), Gemini CLI (`GEMINI_CLI_CUSTOM_HEADERS`) — appended, never assigned, so a value the user set survives |
| `-c` assignment | Codex (`model_providers.<id>.http_headers`) — verified on the wire against codex 0.151.0 |
| registered provider | Pi (`ProviderConfig.headers`) |
| generated provider document | OpenCode, OpenCode 2, Kilo, Command Code, Qwen Code, Crush, Cline |
| **nothing** | Kimi Code, Aider, Droid, Goose — no hook worth trusting; Antigravity is not launched by MCC |

Three of those documents come out of one serialiser (`format_id="opencode"` serves OpenCode,
OpenCode 2 and Kilo) which is a pure function of the model records and cannot know its own harness
id. Rather than change twelve signatures, it writes `MCC_HARNESS_ID_SENTINEL` and the caller resolves
it — the same shape `COMMANDCODE_BASE_URL_SENTINEL` already uses for the base URLs those serialisers
equally cannot know. Proven end to end: all seven document harnesses resolve to their own distinct
id, with no sentinel left on disk.

**2. The user-agent**, where no header arrived. Every non-SDK pattern was copied out of a real
request or the installed CLI's bundle, never invented — a rule written from a product name matches
nothing, and "no rows for this agent" is indistinguishable from "wrong rule for this agent" in a
breakdown.

The header is what makes the answer honest rather than merely plausible:

- **Qwen Code and Pi both send Claude Code's user-agent.** `@qwen-code/qwen-code@0.15.11` builds
  ``claude-cli/${version} (external, cli)`` on its Anthropic path and `@earendil-works/pi-ai` sends
  ``claude-cli/${claudeCodeVersion}``. Seven rows of this log are Qwen Code wearing Claude Code's
  name. No version rule separates them without breaking the day either ships a major, so
  fingerprinting answers `claude` for all three **on purpose** — recorded as `CLAUDE_CLI_COLLISION`
  and pinned by a test — and the header separates them from 6.37.0 on.
- **`claude_agent_sdk` is broken out from `claude`** for the opposite reason: it is a different
  program, and at 80,982 rows (30%) it is the busiest client on this machine.
- **`ai_sdk`, `anthropic_sdk`, `openai_sdk`, `script`** name libraries and one-liners, not agents.
  They are real answers to "who sent this" and can never be registry entries, so they live in a
  closed `NON_REGISTRY_HARNESS_IDS` set with display names, and a test proves nothing else escapes.

## Measured, with the shipped code

Not a prototype: the real `RequestLogStore` was pointed at a `VACUUM INTO` copy of the live log
(2.969 GB, 272,293 rows, no `harness` column) and its own writer thread did the migration.

| step | measured |
| --- | --- |
| `ALTER TABLE requests ADD COLUMN harness TEXT` | 0.002 s (metadata-only in SQLite) |
| backfill, 272,293 rows, 5,000 per committed chunk | **20.5 s** |
| `CREATE INDEX idx_requests_harness_v1 (harness, ts_epoch)` | 0.7 s |
| rollup rebuild at 10 dimensions | **36.5 s** |
| **first start, on the writer thread, never on a request path** | **58.9 s** |
| every later start | **11 ms** |
| rows left unclassified | **0** |
| file growth | 2.969 → 2.988 GB (**+19 MB, +0.6%**) |
| rollup rows | 4,626 → **5,299** (+14.5%, not +12x) |

Why a column *and* a rollup dimension, rather than either alone:

| approach | all-time "requests by harness" |
| --- | --- |
| compute from stored headers at query time | 5.6 s — every Analytics load pays it |
| column + its own index | 756 ms |
| **+ tenth rollup dimension** | **103 ms**, in line with every other card |

Live queries on the migrated copy: `stats(harness="opencode")` 23 ms,
`list_requests(harness="opencode")` **5 ms returning exactly the four rows the user reported as
missing**, `harness_usage(7d)` 197 ms, and the breakdown plans as
`SCAN requests USING COVERING INDEX idx_requests_harness_v1`. `idx_requests_stats_v4` was **not**
widened — the file's own comment records that widening it regressed `fallback_routes` 867 → 1047 ms.

### The backfill histogram

| harness | rows | error rate | tokens in | tokens out |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unknown | 146,658 | 0.7% | 3,401,463,120 | 72,503,673 |
| Claude Agent SDK | 80,982 | 0.2% | 387,532,631 | 25,675,340 |
| Claude Code | 34,924 | 0.5% | 631,033,401 | 22,129,498 |
| Script or curl | 9,708 | 3.2% | 80,500 | 88,950 |
| Crush | 9 | 100.0% | 0 | 0 |
| OpenCode | 4 | 0.0% | 39,359 | 185 |
| Gemini CLI | 2 | 50.0% | 8,402 | 43 |
| Codex CLI | 2 | 0.0% | 580,583 | 27 |
| OpenAI SDK / Droid / Anthropic SDK / Vercel AI SDK | 1 each | | | |

**`Unknown` is 53.9% and always will be.** MCC only began recording inbound headers in 5.36.0, so
every row before 2026-08-20T21:23 has nothing to classify — only 8 rows have headers with no
user-agent in them. Stated in USAGE so the bar does not read as a fault.

## Dashboard

Harness column (position 3 of 12) with a chip carrying the display name; a detail line reading
`OpenCode 1.18.26 (explicit header)` or `(from user-agent)` or `Unknown (no client identification)`;
a Harness filter beside Provider and Model on the 6.13.0 auto-apply pattern, persisted; a
**Requests by harness** breakdown; and `Requests (7d)` on every Coding agents card, counted zeros
included. Labels come from the server as `harness_labels`, so the page never carries a copy of the
registry.

Driven in a real headless Chrome over CDP against the migrated log, not only in jsdom — screenshots
of all five. The filter returns exactly the four OpenCode rows; the detail dialog reads
`Harness → OpenCode 1.18.26 (from user-agent)`.

## Two things found while proving it

- **The jsdom harness had been rendering nothing past the two charts in the requests view.**
  `getContext()` returns null there and `prepareCanvas()` called `setTransform()` on it, so
  `renderReqModelChart` threw and took the rest of `loadRequestsView` with it: the filter datalists,
  all six breakdown panels and the table body were dead in every existing test, and only
  `requestCards` was ever asserted. A no-op 2D context stub revives them; `consoleErrors` 5 → 0, no
  existing test changed outcome, and several previously vacuous areas are now genuinely exercised.
- **Inserting the column before Model moved the error-row colour off its cell.**
  `.req-status-error td:nth-child(5)` → `nth-child(6)`, confirmed in the real browser: `coloured
  cell 6 of 12 = "nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b fallback"`.

## Tests

+62 across storage, API, export, fingerprint, launchers, serialisers and jsdom, including: the
guarded ALTER on a database without the column; a resumable backfill that never redoes work; the
rollup rebuilt when it lacks the dimension and a **versioned marker an old release cannot satisfy**;
`by_harness` equal to the raw `GROUP BY`; the rollup and rows paths agreeing; the 6.13.0 stats
cache-key arity tripwire moved 8 → 9; `harness-usage` not shadowed by `{request_id}`; the
Qwen/Pi collision asserted as `claude`; the sentinel resolved per harness; and the nine jsdom tests.
`tests/api/test_admin_harnesses.py::test_opencode_document_authenticates_with_apikey_alone` kept its
teeth rather than losing them — it now asserts the new `headers` map holds only `x-mcc-harness` and
smuggles no second credential back in the way `Authorization` did before #258.

**9,045 passed, 14 failed** — all 14 pre-existing on this machine (8 websearch, 6 PowerShell
installer), none touched here. `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `ty check` all clean.

## Residual risks

- Five of the sixteen agents have no explicit hook and rely on a user-agent pattern that, for Kimi
  Code, Aider and Goose, has never been observed in a real request. Inert until someone uses them.
- The `claude` bucket over-counts by however many Qwen Code and Pi requests predate this release.
- 53.9% of history is unattributable, permanently.
- The `—` shown when the request log is disabled is implemented but not jsdom-proven; covering it
  needs a third harness run behind its own env flag.
- `iter_export_rows` still has no `local` parameter — a known 6.13.0 gap this does not close.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commit.message:
feat(analytics): name the coding agent behind every request

The report was "Analytics doesn't register requests from OpenCode". It does.
Four rows of the live log carry `opencode/1.18.26 ai-sdk/provider-utils/4.0.46
runtime/bun/1.3.14`, POST /v1/messages, nous_portal, meituan/longcat-2.0:free,
all four success. They were invisible only because nothing in the table, the
cards or the detail dialog ever named the client that sent them, so they read
as four more rows among 128,000 Claude Code ones on the same models.

So record it. `requests.harness` is filled at capture time from two signals,
explicit first: the `x-mcc-harness` header MCC's own launchers now write into
the configuration they generate, and failing that the user-agent, matched
against a table whose every non-SDK entry was copied out of a real request
rather than guessed from a product name. Eleven of the sixteen agents can carry
the header -- Claude Code and Gemini CLI through an environment variable, Codex
through a `-c` assignment, Pi through its registered provider, and seven more
through the provider document MCC writes for them. The other five have no hook
worth trusting and stay on user-agent alone.

The header is what makes the answer honest rather than merely plausible. Qwen
Code and Pi both send `claude-cli/<their own version>` on their Anthropic path
-- seven rows of this log are Qwen Code wearing Claude Code's name -- and no
version rule could separate them without breaking the day either ships a major.
Fingerprinting answers `claude` for all three on purpose; the header separates
them from here on. `agent-sdk/` is broken out as its own harness for the
opposite reason: it is a different program from the CLI and, at 80,982 rows,
the busiest client on this machine.

Storage is a column plus a rollup dimension, because the user opens the
all-time view. Computing it from the stored headers at query time costs 5.6 s a
page load; the column with its own index costs 756 ms; the tenth rollup
dimension costs 103 ms, in line with every other card. Measured on a copy of
the real 2.97 GB / 272,293-row log, driven by the shipped store: ALTER 0.002 s,
backfill 20.5 s in chunks of 5,000, index 0.7 s, rollup rebuild 36.5 s -- 58.9 s
once, on the writer thread, then 11 ms on every later start. The rollup grew
4,626 -> 5,299 rows and the file by 19 MB.

Two consequences stated in USAGE rather than left to look like faults. Headers
have only been recorded since 5.36.0, so 146,658 of those rows -- 53.9% -- have
nothing to classify and read as Unknown for ever. And a model that appears
nowhere in Analytics never reached the proxy at all: no `ling` request exists
anywhere in this log, which is a launcher question and not an Analytics one.

The dashboard gains a Harness column, a detail line that says whether the
answer was stated or inferred, a filter beside Provider and Model, a Requests
by harness breakdown, and Requests (7d) on every Coding agents card. All four
export formats carry the column and can group by it.

Two things found while proving it. The jsdom harness had been rendering nothing
past the two charts in the requests view -- getContext() returns null there and
prepareCanvas() threw, killing the rest of the function -- so the filters, all
six breakdowns and the table body were untested in every existing test; a
no-op 2D context stub revives them and takes consoleErrors 5 -> 0. And
inserting the column before Model moved the error-row colour off its cell,
which nth-child(6) fixes and a real browser confirms.

test: clear the mirrored client fingerprint between tests

`install_fingerprint` writes a ContextVar the Anthropic subscription provider
reads to reproduce the caller's own headers upstream, and `build_capture` sets
it as a side effect. Under xdist the next test on that worker inherited it, so
a fixture user-agent from the new capture tests reached
`test_oauth_headers_are_the_claude_code_set` and it asserted
`something-nobody-has-seen/1 == claude-cli/2.1.258 (external, cli)` -- on CI's
shard order only, which is why the same suite was green locally.

The leak predates this branch; nothing but a second suite calling `build_capture`
was needed to reach it. Clearing it around every test fixes it for every future
one too, rather than asking each new test that captures a request to remember.
